title: One key shape for per-IP limits
evidence: The app routes key their per-IP limits on the /64 bucket (ipBucket in app-gate.server.ts; app-routes.server.ts, api.chat.ts web turns), while other per-IP limiters key on the address as read (api.feedback, api.events, api.ab, api.measurements, api.google-token, api.lab-import-v2). Use one key shape for all. From the PR 1613 review. Design note docs/drafts/s-21-ip-key-design.md (owner rulings 2026-11-14). PR 1a of the series (1665): address keys normalised before use, the shape of the forwarded header counted (numbers only), an over-limit quota charge refused before it touches the map (US-52 AC4g-AC4i). PR 1b (1667): the forwarded hop read only where Fly writes its entry (AC4j), merging after the count is read. No limiter moved onto the bucket yet. Verify at batch end: a normal storefront chat and lab upload are not refused; the 429 rate on those routes does not jump; the hourly forwarded-shape line appears in the logs
